grade.first_issue: After proving continuity only at points of the range R_f, the submission asserts that injectivity makes f strictly increasing. Injectivity implies monotonicity only when continuity on the entire domain has been established; continuity merely on R_f is insufficient.
grade.summary: The solution correctly identifies and verifies f(x)=x+c with c≥0, and it derives the important orbit identity ε(f(y))=ε(y), the nonnegativity ε≥0, injectivity, and a useful estimate on ε over the range. However, the uniqueness proof then relies on an invalid monotonicity inference. The subsequent claim that any jump propagates with size 2^nδ is neither proved nor generally justified by the functional identity, so global continuity and the assertion that R_f is an interval remain unsupported. Consequently, the final constancy argument cannot be applied. Repair requires a new load-bearing argument comparing forward orbits and excluding coexistence of zero and positive defects.
strengths: Correctly squares and combines the original inequalities.
Correctly verifies every function f(x)=x+c for c≥0.
Correctly obtains f(f(y))+y=2f(y), orbit invariance of ε, and ε(y)≥0.
Correctly proves injectivity and derives |ε(x)-ε(z)|≤(√x-√z)^2 for x,z in R_f.
Correctly observes that the displayed squeeze establishes continuity at each point of R_f.

errors.description: The inference from injectivity plus continuity on R_f to strict monotonicity is false and is essential to the remainder of the proof.
The asserted propagation of a jump to f^{(n)}(x_0) with size 2^nδ is unproved; the vague exponential-versus-linear comparison therefore does not establish continuity on the full domain.
Without global continuity and monotonicity, R_f has not been shown to be an interval, so the partition argument proving ε constant on R_f—and hence everywhere—has no valid foundation.
